  • Ans.
  • The Eddington luminosity is the maximum luminosity a star (or any radiating object) can
  • have such that the outward radiation pressure balances the inward gravitational force.
  • Beyond this limit, radiation can push matter away from the star.

questions.question: Describe the inverse square law. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the inverse square law. [U] / [CO1]
  • Ans. An isotropic source emits energy equally in all directions. Imagine two spheres, S1 and S
  • with radius r1 and r near the source. By conservation of energy, the total energy passing
  • through S1 must be the same as that passing through S.
  • The energy radiated ,dE = F dA dt.
  • F (r1) ⋅ 4πr12 = F (r) ⋅ 4πr2
  • If sphere S1 is fixed:
  • F (r) = constant/r2
  • ⇒ F(r) ∝ 1/r²
  • The radiative flux from a source decreases inversely as the square of the distance from the
  • source.This is the Inverse Square Law.
  • Give 5 marks to full explanation.Law / Equation only-2 marks.

questions.question: Describe how the expression for mean intensity is obtained under equilibrium condition. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how the expression for mean intensity is obtained under equilibrium
  • Ans.Under thermodynamic equilibrium, the specific intensity Iν is exactly equal to the Planck
  • function Bν(T).Since the field is isotropic in equilibrium:
  • Iν = Bν(T) …………..1
  • ∫ Iν dΩ = Bν(T) ∫ dΩ = 4π Bν(T) …….2
  • Substituting this into the mean intensity formula:
  • Jν = (1 / 4π) (4π Bν(T)) = Bν(T).........3
  • Equation 1 only - 2marks. Complete steps- 5 marks. Mean intensity Jν = 1/4π∫ IνdΩ -2marks

questions.question: Give a detailed account of stellar structure and the fundamental equations governing stellar equilibrium and energy transport. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Give a detailed account of stellar structure and the fundamental equations governing stellar
  • equilibrium and energy transport.
  • Ans.
  • stellar structure refers to the radial variation of physical quantities inside a star, such as:
  • ● Pressure
  • ● Density
  • ● Temperature
  • ● Luminosity
  • ● Enclosed mass
  • (2 mark)
  • Hydrostatic equilibrium
  • Hydrostatic equilibrium is the primary condition for stellar stability.
  • This equation states that inside a star, inward gravity is exactly balanced by the outward
  • pressure gradient.
  • (1.5 mark if either equation with terms explained or the statement is given)
  • Virial Theorem
  • The Virial Theorem for a Star in Equilibrium
  • For a star in hydrostatic equilibrium:
  • 2K+U=0
  • where
  • ● K= total internal kinetic energy (thermal energy of gas particles)
  • ● U= total gravitational potential energy
  • (1.5 mark if either equation with terms explained or the statement is given)

questions.question: Discuss formation and evolution of GMCs. / [CO4] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss formation and evolution of GMCs. [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans :-
  • ● Dense regions of gas and dust in the interstellar medium (ISM) where physical conditions
  • such as temperature, density, and mass vary widely known as Interstellar clouds. They are
  • Classified into Diffuse / Translucent molecular Clouds & Giant Molecular Clouds (GMCs).
  • Giant Molecular Clouds are the regions of star formation. The regions of gas and dust in the
  • ISM are Molecular Clouds.The main characteristics of GMC are Large size with typical
  • diameters 50pc,Cloud collapses and stars form due to gravity, Temperature: ~15 K, Number
  • density: 1×108 to 3×108 m−33 (Density 1020 times of a typical star), Hundreds of thousands of
  • times heavier than the Sun (105 ), Size: ~50 pc
  • ● A cloud begins to collapse when gravity overcomes internal pressure.This condition is
  • described by the Jeans Mass: If Mcloud>MJ. When the collapsing GMC attains high density, it
  • becomes gravitationally unstable and breaks up into smaller pieces.When fragmentation happens
  • the turbulence inside the cloud, Shock waves from nearby supernovae, Galactic rotation, Magnetic
  • field effects. Each fragment can form A single star, A binary star system,A small star clusterThe
  • fragmentation of collapsing clouds leads to the formation of protostars − pre-stellar objects which
  • are hot enough to radiate infrared radiation but not hot enough to generate energy by nuclear
  • fusion.
  • ● Fragmentation of collapsing cloud leads to a stage when a protostar is formed and its interior
  • attains hydrostatic equilibrium.
  • ● The interior of the protostar at this stage becomes almost convective
  • ● The stellar object so formed is called a pre-main sequence star.
  • ( Definition of GMC with any three properties give full marks)
